w:r.w:t: The Terminal Tracking Application is a purpose-built, standalone web application designed for Terminal Distributor — a global payment terminal distributor managing serialised payment devices across a worldwide warehouse network. The application serves as the master system of record for terminal serial number states, inventory counts, order management, and cost tracking.

The core problem is visibility: Terminal Distributor currently lacks a unified system to answer fundamental operational questions — where is a specific terminal right now, what state is it in, is it available, when will it arrive, and how much has it cost? This PRD defines the requirements to build a lean, web-based solution that resolves these gaps.
The application is designed in two releases:
Core tracking, master data, inbound/outbound order management, return and repair flows, warehouse tooling, and basic analytics.
Demand and supply planning, inventory repositioning, purchase prediction, alerting framework, work order management, claims management, and API integration with external systems.

Technology: React + Vite frontend, Python FastAPI backend, SQLite (local) upgradeable to PostgreSQL (server), Tailwind CSS with e2open colour palette. Role-based access control with JWT authentication. Icon-based left sidebar navigation.

Terminal Distributor is a global distributor of payment terminals operating warehouses and forward stocking locations (FSLs) across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, and South America. Their portfolio includes ~486 SKUs: payment terminals (serialised), serialised accessories (pin pads, contactless readers), and non-serialised accessories (cables, SIM cards, receipt rolls, batteries).

Terminal Distributor manages high-value serialised payment devices through a complex lifecycle: from purchase order and inbound receipt, through staging and key injection, to outbound shipment to customers, and back via return and repair. Tracking today is fragmented across spreadsheets and disconnected systems. The result is a lack of real-time serial-level visibility, inability to confirm ATP dates, and no unified cost tracking per terminal.
The application must fulfil the following business objectives:
Monitor the location and status of every terminal by serial number at all times.
Real-time counts of terminals by product and by location, across all states.
Track processing costs and unit costs per terminal and at aggregate level, normalised to a reporting currency.
Identify locations where terminals are missing or in overflow and support repositioning decisions.
Enable multiple business personas (Supply Planner, Warehouse User, Repair Centre, Supplier) to collaborate on a single order or serial number record.
Allow planning of terminal transfers from one warehouse to another.
Monitor average dwell time per state, average repair time, transit times, and customer return behaviour.
Manage the full return and repair lifecycle at serial number level, including Scrap/End of Lifecycle.
On outbound orders, confirm delivery date and fulfilling location based on current inventory, transit times, and assembly times.
Forecast new purchase orders from suppliers based on demand signals and lead times.
Manage all reference data — products, BOMs, suppliers, warehouses, transit times, customers, states, activity costs, exchange rates, and order numbering rules.

Count of available, in-transit, in-repair, and total units per SKU.
All terminals in EXPECTING state. Shows: serial, product, PO reference, carrier, ETA, destination warehouse.
Single serial number view: current state, location, full state history genealogy (state, location,
Count of non-serialised accessories per location per product. Editable by Warehouse User.
Ad-hoc ATP check: enter product code + quantity → system returns available location, expected ship date, expected delivery date.
All purchase orders with status, supplier, destination, qty ordered vs. received. Filterable by status.
PO header + lines table: product, qty ordered, qty expected (serials uploaded), qty received. Shows carrier, ETA, shipment reference.
All outbound orders across all types (Sales, Rental, Replacement, Distribution). Filterable by type, status, customer.
Order header (ID, type, customer/destination, status), order lines, allocated serials, ATP result, shipment details, status timeline.
All Return Orders with status, customer, reason, linked Replacement Order ID.
Return header, serial numbers, reason, inspection outcome (Defective/Scrap), linked Replacement and Repair Orders.
All Repair Orders with status, serial numbers, repair centre, estimated return date.
Supply Planner, Warehouse User, Repair Centre
Repair header, serial numbers, repair centre, status, actual cost entry, estimated return date, send-back confirmation.
List of all products. Filterable by type, serialised, BOM flag. Links to Product Detail.

assignments, authorised repair centres, applicable countries, costs, interchangeable products.
Supplier list with country, products supplied.
Location list. Each location has code, name, type (selectable), country, reporting currency.

List of assembly times per location in days. Used in ATP when kit components need consolidation.
Customer list with type, country, credit rating.
Configurable state list: code, display name, warehouse type, valid predecessor states, acting role. Add/deactivate.
Cost entries per state per location, optionally per product/BOM. Currency per entry.

Configure order ID prefix and zero-padding per order type (e.g., SO######, RN######).
Create, edit, and deactivate users. Assign roles. Reset passwords.
Charts: inventory by state, dwell times, repair times, transit times, order fulfillment rate, return rate.
Upload zone with template downloads for each upload type. Shows last upload result and downloadable error report.
All master data is managed by the Admin role. Excel bulk upload is supported for all entities for initial population and ongoing maintenance. All entities support Active/Inactive flag.
The product master and BOM configuration are a single entity. Each product record contains:
Boolean — if Yes, tracked at serial number level; if No, tracked by count only
Multi-select list of countries (from a country reference list) where this product is applicable. Replaces free-text Regions field.
Multi-select links to other Product records in the Product Master — not free text. Used for substitution during ATP.
Boolean — if Yes, this product is a kit/box containing multiple components
If Is BOM = Yes: a list of component product codes with quantities. Admin can add or remove components from the BOM configuration.
Many-to-many link to Supplier Master — multiple suppliers per product
List of Location records (type = Repair Centre) that are authorised to repair this product. Used in Repair Order routing.
Excel bulk upload supports initial population. Product Code must be unique. BOM component product codes must already exist in the master.
Each supplier record contains: Supplier Code, Supplier Name, Country, City, Contact Details (optional), and a read-only list of Products Supplied (derived from Product Master linkage).
Unique short code (e.g., Oostrum, DHLAU, FSLUK)
Selectable from a configurable type list (maintained by Admin). Default types: Warehouse, FSL, Repair Centre, Supplier. Admin can add or rename types without code changes.
The currency to which all activity costs at this location are normalised for reporting (e.g., EUR for Oostrum, USD for Memphis). Set per location.
Transit times are maintained as a standalone entity, separate from the Location Master. Each transit time record covers a specific lane:
Number of calendar days for this lane and mode

Lanes are maintained in a grid view (From × To). If no lane is defined, the system uses a configurable global fallback lead time (default: 14 days, set by Admin). The transit time master feeds the ATP calculation engine.
Transit time applies to: warehouse-to-warehouse (Distribution Orders), warehouse-to-customer (Sales/Rental/Replacement Orders), and supplier-to-warehouse (inbound ETA estimation).

Assembly time is the number of days required to consolidate BOM components at a single location before shipment, when not all components are co-located. Configured per location (e.g., Oostrum = 2 days). Used in ATP calculation for kit orders where sourcing from multiple locations is required.
Optional — for risk flagging on outbound orders
Terminal states are configurable master data, managed exclusively by Admin. States apply only to serialised products. Admin can:
Add a new state (code, display name, description, warehouse type classification)
Define which role(s) may trigger a transition into each state
Default state set included with Release 1:
PO creation / serial number file upload
PO raised; serial assigned by supplier; not yet received at warehouse
VAS activities in progress (firmware, kitting, battery charge, packaging)
Delivered to and confirmed by customer
Delivery attempt failed at customer location
Warehouse User: Return Order receipt (Defective outcome)
At repair centre; repair in progress
Repair Centre: repair complete + sent back
Returned from repair; awaiting quality check
Refurbished and available to sell or distribute
Terminal scrapped, destroyed, or end of
lifecycle. Traceability ends. Terminal is never re-activated.
Defines the standard cost of each warehouse or logistics activity per location, forming the basis for per-terminal cost tracking.
The location where the activity occurs
The state the cost is associated with
Product-level cost override when cost varies by SKU or kit
Currency specific to this location's activities

For IN_REPAIR activities, the Activity Cost Master holds a standard estimate only. The Repair Centre user enters the actual repair cost upon job completion, which overrides the standard cost for that specific terminal.
Exchange rates are used to normalise costs recorded in various currencies into a single reporting currency for each warehouse. Each record contains:
Date from which this rate is valid

The system applies the exchange rate effective on the date of each state transition activity to normalise costs. If no specific rate is found for an exact date, the most recent prior effective rate is used.
The Admin configures the ID convention for each order type. Default conventions (all configurable):

Every serialised terminal is tracked at serial number level. The current record contains the terminal's present state, location, and references. The state history is a separate 1:N child entity — one terminal has many history entries, each immutable:
Unique identifier assigned by the manufacturer
Current terminal state (from configurable state set)
Current warehouse or customer/repair location code
Purchase Order ID and PO Line ID (genesis reference)
Outbound Order ID and line (if applicable)
If terminal has been moved or dispatched
Running total of all activity costs, normalised to reporting currency
Location where the state change occurred (warehouse code or customer/repair centre reference)
Timezone of the warehouse/location where the change was recorded
User ID or 'API' — who triggered the transition
Optional free-text notes attached to this transition

Non-serialised accessories are tracked by quantity per location. States: Received (in warehouse, not yet available) and Available. Quantity adjustments are made manually by Warehouse Users or via mass upload.

The ATP Query allows a Supply Planner to check, before creating an order, whether a product and quantity can be fulfilled and by when. Input: product code (or BOM code) + required quantity. Output: fulfilling location, ship date, delivery date. If BOM, all components are checked. If kit assembly is required (components from multiple locations), assembly time is added to the lead time calculation.
Purchase Orders have a Header and one or more Lines. A single PO can contain multiple product lines from the same supplier.
PO Number (auto-generated per numbering convention), Supplier, Destination Warehouse, Order Date, Expected Arrival Date, Status, Notes
Line Number, Product Code, Quantity Ordered, Quantity Expected (serials declared by supplier), Quantity Received (confirmed by warehouse)
PO created but not yet issued to supplier
Supplier has declared the serial numbers (uploaded the inbound file). Serials are in EXPECTING state. Not yet received at warehouse.
At least one serial confirmed received; not all lines complete

When a supplier ships goods, they provide a file containing the serial numbers of shipped terminals linked to the PO. This file can be uploaded by: the Supplier (via their limited-access portal), the Supply Planner, or the Warehouse User.
Supplier's shipment or delivery note reference
Name of the carrier handling the shipment
Expected date at the destination warehouse
The user selects the relevant PO before uploading the file, or the PO ID is included in the file.
The system parses each row and creates a serial number record with state = EXPECTING, linked to the PO and the carrier/ETA details.
Uniqueness check: a serial number is considered a duplicate if the same SerialNumber + Supplier combination already exists in the system. Duplicate rows are rejected with a per-row error report.
Non-duplicate serials are created; the PO status updates to Expected.
The Expecting view is updated to show: serial number, product, PO reference, inbound shipment reference, carrier, ETA, and destination warehouse.
The import template (Excel) is downloadable from the Upload Centre view.

The PO Detail view shows a three-column qty summary per line: Qty Ordered | Qty Expected (serials uploaded) | Qty Received (confirmed by warehouse). This allows the warehouse user to identify any shortfall at a glance.
Warehouse User opens the PO Detail view from the Expecting view.
User confirms receipt — individually per serial, or via mass confirmation of all expected serials under the PO.
Confirmed serials transition from EXPECTING to QUARANTINE. Receipt date and location are recorded.
The PO line Qty Received count increments. PO status updates to Partially Received or Fully Received.
If the received quantity is less than the Qty Expected, the remaining serials stay in EXPECTING state. The delta is visible in the PO Detail view.

If the received quantity is less than expected (missing) or terminals arrive damaged, the Warehouse User can create a Claim against the supplier or logistics carrier. Claim types (e.g., Missing, Damaged, Wrong Item) are configurable by Admin. Claim management is a Release 2 feature.
Outbound Orders are created by Supply Planners and represent any movement of terminals away from a warehouse — to customers, to other warehouses, as rentals, or as replacements.
Standard sale of terminals to a merchant, shop, distributor, or partner
Same customer as linked Return Order
Replacement of a defective terminal returned by a customer. Auto-drafted on Return Order initiation.
Temporary deployment with defined rental period and fee. Terminal expected back at end of rental period.
Inter-warehouse transfer. Destination selected from a dropdown of Location Master warehouse codes.
Order created but not yet submitted. Editable by Supply Planner.
Order submitted. Visible in warehouse queue.
System has allocated specific serial numbers to this order.
Warehouse User has acknowledged and is physically picking.
Carrier, Tracking Number, Shipped Date, Estimated Arrival Date, Shipping Cost.
Delivery confirmed (carrier POD or customer confirmation).
Status Delivery Failed if carrier cannot deliver. Warehouse User or Supply Planner initiates a retry or triggers a Return flow.
Orders can be cancelled from Draft through In Picking. Once Shipped, cancellation is not permitted.
Every outbound order triggers an ATP (Available-to-Promise) check. The ATP engine:
Checks AVAILABLE inventory of each order line at the preferred fulfillment location (or nearest available location).
For BOM/kit products: expands the BOM into components and checks each component's availability.
If all components are co-located: ATP date = today + transit time (from Transit Time Master) to customer.

If components are split across locations: the engine identifies the missing components, checks alternate locations, and calculates: transit time to consolidate at fulfillment location + assembly time (from Assembly Time Master) + transit time to customer.
The ATP result is displayed to the Supply Planner showing: fulfilling location, expected ship date, expected delivery date.

The Supply Planner can adjust order quantity or date. Each adjustment triggers a recalculation. If the requested date is not achievable, a red warning message is displayed: 'ATP infeasible — earliest possible delivery is [date].' The Supply Planner can acknowledge the warning and proceed with their own date (override decision recorded).
Specific serial number allocation happens at the Allocated status, not at order creation. ATP confirms count feasibility only.

When components must be sourced from multiple locations, the system will in Release 2 automatically generate a Work Order sent to the relevant Warehouse User, instructing them to prepare the assembly.
Rental orders include additional fields beyond standard Sales:
Duration of rental. Defaults to 12 months; editable per order.
Automatically calculated as Shipped Date + Rental Period. Tracked and visible in the Order Detail view.
Rental expiry alerting (e.g., notification 1 week before expected return date) is planned for Release 2 as part of the Alerting Framework.
Replacement Orders are auto-drafted by the system when a Return Order reaches Initiated status (see 8.5.1). The auto-drafted Replacement Order is pre-populated with:
Same customer as the Return Order
Same product as the returned terminal (or the best available alternative product if the same product has zero AVAILABLE inventory)
Same source warehouse as the originating outbound order

The auto-draft appears in the Supply Planner's queue for review and issuance. The Supply Planner can adjust product, quantity, or source location before issuing. The Replacement Order is linked to the Return Order by reference and both are visible from each other's detail views.
A Return Order (RExxxxxx) is created when a customer returns a terminal. Return Order fields:
Defective | End of Rental | End of Lifecycle | Wrong Item | Other
Initiated | In Transit | Received | Inspected | Closed
Set at Inspected status — Defective or Scrap

Initiated: Return Order created. System immediately auto-drafts a Replacement Order (same product, same customer, same source warehouse; alternative product if same product unavailable). Supply Planner is notified to review and issue the replacement draft.
In Transit: Customer has shipped the terminal back.
Received: Warehouse User confirms physical receipt. Terminal serial number state transitions to DEFECT.
Inspected: Warehouse User inspects the terminal and sets the Inspection Outcome:
Outcome = Defective → Warehouse User initiates a Repair Order (RRxxxxxx). Terminal state moves to UNDER_INVESTIGATION.
Outcome = Scrap → Terminal state transitions to SCRAP/DESTROYED. Terminal traceability ends. The terminal record is closed and marked permanently inactive. It cannot be reactivated.
A Repair Order (RRxxxxxx) is created from the Return Order Inspected step or directly from inventory for a defective terminal. Key fields and flow:
Selected from the list of Authorised Repair Centres defined on the Product Master for this product. Not all repair centres service all products.
Expected date back at the originating warehouse (set by Repair Centre user on confirmation)
Same warehouse the terminal was received from (editable if needed)
Dispatched | Received at Repair Centre | In Repair | Completed | Returned
Entered by Repair Centre user upon job completion (amount + currency)
Warehouse User creates Repair Order, selects authorised repair centre for the product, and dispatches. Terminal state → TRANSIT_TO_REPAIR.
Repair Centre User confirms receipt. Terminal state → IN_REPAIR.
Repair Centre User completes repair. Enters: actual repair cost, repair notes, outcome (Repaired or Beyond Repair), and confirms shipment back to warehouse with estimated date of arrival.
Outcome = Repaired → Terminal state → QUARANTINE_REFURBISHED at the originating warehouse upon return receipt.
Outcome = Beyond Repair → Terminal state → SCRAP/DESTROYED. Traceability ends.
Warehouse User receives terminal back and moves it to AVAILABLE_REFURBISHED after quality check.
SCRAP and DESTROYED are the same terminal state. Once a terminal enters this state it cannot be reactivated or used in any order.

The Mass Upload feature allows Warehouse Users (and Supply Planners where applicable) to process high-volume state changes and confirmations without serial-by-serial data entry. All uploads are logged in the audit trail.
Bulk confirm receipt of all or selected serials under a PO. Serials move from EXPECTING to QUARANTINE.
Serial Number, PO ID, Receipt Date (default: today), Location (default: user's default location)
Bulk update of any state that Warehouse Users are authorised to set: ENCRYPTION_KEY_LOADED, STAGING, AVAILABLE, AVAILABLE_REFURBISHED, and others as configured in State Master.
Serial Number, New State, Date (default: today), Location (default: user's location), Notes (optional)
Confirm shipment of multiple orders (mix of types, e.g. 100 terminals across several Sales and Distribution orders) in one action.
Order ID, Serial Number, Shipped Date (default: today), Carrier, Tracking Number, Shipping Cost
Adjust counts of non-serialised accessories per location.
Product Code, Location, State (Received/Available), Quantity, Date
Create new EXPECTING serial records linked to a PO. See 8.3.2 for full specification.
Serial Number, Product Code, PO ID, Shipment Reference, Carrier, ETA, Carrier Tracking Ref
Include a downloadable template Excel file per upload type (available from the Upload Centre view)
Return a per-row error report if any rows fail (e.g., serial not found, duplicate, invalid state transition)
Are logged in the system audit trail: uploading user, timestamp, upload type, filename, total records, successful records, failed records
Count of terminals in each state across all locations. Filterable by product, location, stock type.
Quantity per product per warehouse/FSL. Serialised and non-serialised combined.
Average days a terminal spends in each state. Identifies process bottlenecks.
Average days from TRANSIT_TO_REPAIR to QUARANTINE_REFURBISHED, per repair centre.
Average days in transit per lane by transport mode.
Percentage of orders delivered on or before the ATP-committed delivery date.
Volume of Return Orders by customer, reason, and product over a rolling period.
Total accumulated activity costs per serial number normalised to reporting currency. Exportable to Excel.
Active rental orders with expected return dates, filterable by customer and product.
The application will be architecturally ready for future integration with the TERMINAL DISTRIBUTOR Logistics API. In Release 1, the API module exists as a structural placeholder:
Stub endpoint and configuration screen for pulling PO, serial number, distribution, and dispatch data from an external API.
Stub for pushing state changes and order updates back to an external system.

The API module stub is not activated in R1. Schema, endpoint configuration, and data mapping layer are prepared. Admin has a configuration screen to set the API base URL, credentials, and field mappings. Activation happens in R2.
Any inventory list view must load within 3 seconds for up to 10,000 serial number records. Search and filter results must return within 2 seconds.
Designed for hundreds of active serial numbers and dozens of concurrent orders in R1. Database schema supports migration to PostgreSQL for larger scale without application code changes.

All state transitions are logged immutably with timestamp (including timezone), user, and source. No state change is permitted without a valid preceding state per the transition rules in the State Configuration master.
Complete, immutable state history per serial number and complete status history per order, permanently stored and viewable.
Username/password authentication. Passwords hashed (bcrypt). Role-based access control enforced at API level. JWT session tokens with configurable expiry. HTTPS when deployed to server.
Excel upload for all master data entities and all operational upload types. All list views exportable to Excel.
Chrome, Edge, Firefox (latest 2 versions). No mobile requirement in R1.
R1: runs locally via a single start command (e.g., ./start.sh). R2: deployable to Linux server with documented setup instructions.
UI in English. Currency fields support multi-currency with exchange rate normalisation. Date/time fields store timezone.
All activity costs are stored in their native currency. For reporting and the accumulated cost total, costs are converted to the warehouse's reporting currency using the Exchange Rate Master.
Fast component-based UI. Vite provides lean local dev server. Hot reload for iteration speed.
Utility-first CSS with e2open colour palette (navy #003087, blue #0075C2, orange #F7941D) as custom design tokens.
One icon per module. Active state highlighted in blue. Collapsed by default, expandable.
Modern, high-performance Python API. Auto-generates OpenAPI docs. Async-capable. Easy to extend for API integration module.
Database-agnostic ORM. SQLite → PostgreSQL migration requires only a connection string change.
SQLite requires zero infrastructure for local deployment. PostgreSQL migration is a one-step upgrade for server hosting.
Stateless auth with role claims in token. Refresh token for session persistence.
Excel file parsing and export for all upload types and data exports.
Placeholder endpoints prepared for R2 Logistics API GET/POST operations.
